cohort: The study participants were 22,150 individuals (13,297 in Brazil and 8,853 in the US) born with orofacial clefts between 2017 and 2021.
finding: The frequency of risk factors and adverse birth health conditions associated with being born with orofacial clefts was significantly higher in the Brazilian cohort compared to the United States.
mod_finding: Newborns with clefts in Brazil were significantly more likely to be born by cesarean section compared to the United States cohort.
birth_weight: Birthweight was measured as a birth health condition for all included individuals; newborns with clefts in Brazil were more likely to have low birth weight.
gest_age: Gestational age was measured as a birth health condition for all included individuals; newborns with clefts in Brazil were more likely to be premature.
